questions_and_answers.question: They have just come out of mass.
I have just finished my homework.
Jean has just asked why they can’t go.

answers.text: Jean acaba de preguntar por qué no pueden ir.

questions_and_answers.question: Bob has just told Jean they can’t go to mass.

answers.text: Bob acaba de decirle a Jean que no pueden ir a misa.

questions_and_answers.question: They have just gone to the cathedral.

answers.text: Acaban de ir a la catedral.

questions_and_answers.question: I have just drunk a coffee.
We have just seen the Foreign Affairs Office.

answers.text: Acabamos de ver el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores.

questions_and_answers.question: She has just walked through the park.

answers.text: Ella acaba de pasear por el parque.

articles.text: Spanish expresses the idea of having just done something using 'acabar de' + infinitive. Translate the following sentences using this construction.

metadata.instructions: Translate the following sentences into Spanish using 'acabar de' + infinitive.
